answer: An identity that tries to mirror a legitimate agent's behavior still lacks history, forcing attackers to fund and sustain many staked identities across epochs, making sybil costs exceed any reward. Each agent must stake tokens and submit a signed pulse every epoch; the protocol's scoring kernel weights votes by stake age and uptime, so freshly spun-up identities carry almost no weight. From qwe0006's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
